story: Alex sat on the porch with a cup of tea, the steam curling into the morning air. His breath came steady and slow, matching the rhythm of the wind through the trees. He watched a cat pad across the yard, tail high, and smiled to himself. The warmth of the sun on his skin and the quiet hum of the world around him settled into his bones. He didn’t rush, didn’t reach—he simply let the moment stretch, like a well-worn blanket wrapped around his shoulders.

Alex sat on the porch, bare feet resting on the worn wooden slats, toes curled slightly against the cool morning air. The sun had just begun to stretch over the hills, painting the sky in soft golds and pinks. He sipped his tea slowly, watching the steam rise in lazy spirals before vanishing. A breeze tugged gently at the corner of his shirt, and he let it, not moving to steady the fabric. Birds called in the distance, and Alex smiled as he listened, his breath steady and full.

Alex sat on the porch with a cup of tea, watching the steam curl into the cool morning air. His breath moved in steady rhythm, matching the slow creak of the swing beneath him. Distant birds called to each other, and the leaves rustled without hurry. He let his eyes drift shut for a moment, savoring the warmth of the sun on his face. When he opened them again, the world felt still and full, as if time had paused just for him.
